tagline: A short shore road where the mountain men once met.
intro: US 89 comes south from the Idaho line to Garden City, where the byway turns onto SR-30 and keeps to the shore as far as Laketown. The water is the turquoise that earned the lake its name as the Caribbean of the Rockies, a color owed to limestone held in suspension.
Mormon settlers built Garden City, Pickelville and Laketown along the shore after 1863. The road began in 1990 as the Laketown Scenic Byway and reached north to the state line in 2002.

moments.title: Bear Lake
moments.text: A lake at least 250,000 years old, formed by a sinking fault that is still at work, slowly deepening it along the eastern side.

moments.title: Garden City
moments.text: In 1903 the first automobile journey across the United States stopped here, some while before the town became known for raspberry milkshakes in summer.

moments.title: Laketown
moments.text: The trappers' rendezvous of 1827 met near here, and Jedediah Smith arrived back from California to a considerable bustle, he and his party having been given up as lost.

sources.label: Utah Admin. Code R926-13-4, State Scenic Byways (LII)
